title: Space no longer plays an audio take on the run desk, and M spawn MV was never built
instrument: a keymap/legend parity test (board-render: legend caps == handled verbs) plus a live spec pressing Space on an audio run
body:
## Summary
The `board.cull` keymap still carries `play` (Space) and `spawn-mv` (M) under `when: audio`, but no cull desk answers either.

## Description
The row desk's `play` handler left with it in 43627d5e (git show: `play: () => play(cur)` removed from MatrixCull.tsx); `spawn-mv` has had no handler anywhere since the keymap landed in 33b21d2a (`git log -S'"spawn-mv":'` = 0 handlers). 6bc3490f stopped the legend drawing them (packages/ui/src/components/cull/CullFoot.tsx `cullFacts`), so the keys are now honestly absent; keymap.test.ts:134 and :218 still pin both rows. Whether Space should play the take under the cursor on the mosaic (RunCard draws a waveform, no <audio>; VariantCard has <audio controls> only in an opened run) and whether M should spawn a music video from a take is the operator's call.

## Flow
- open an audio packet (lane audio) on the Board
- press Space or M: nothing happens (useRunDesk.ts useKeys binds neither verb)
- decide: restore play in useRunDesk (and arm `audio` in cullFacts), build spawn-mv, or delete the two rows and their keymap tests

## Expected impact
The operator either gets the audition key back on the desk or the keymap stops carrying two verbs no screen implements. Could break keymap.test.ts if the rows go.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the audio cull desk has an audition key, or the keymap holds no dead verbs
Before: 2 bound verbs with 0 handlers
After: unmeasured; which arm is a product call
Method: probe - grep of handlers; the rung above needs the direction first
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
packages/ui/src/keymap/bindings.ts:75-76
packages/ui/src/components/cull/useRunDesk.ts:204-237 (no play/spawn-mv)
git show 43627d5e | grep '^-.*play: () => play(cur)'

title: CullTile and Zoom have no screen left but /kit
instrument: grep of importers (today: only app/(studio)/kit/BoardKit.tsx) and the kit census of shapes
body:
## Summary
The CullTile component and the Zoom lens are mounted only by the /kit specimens since the run grid replaced the row desk.

## Description
`grep -rn 'CullTile\b|Zoom\b'` over app/ and packages/: the only mounts are app/(studio)/kit/BoardKit.tsx:116-157. Production draws RunCard / VariantCard / RunModal; it imports only `kindOf`, `TileMedia` and `spokenTile` from CullTile.tsx. The INVENTORY row still describes CullTile and Zoom as live ("the lens over a desk"), and ~38 of Cull.module.css's 40 classes serve them. Zoom's legend (ZOOM_KEYS keep/reject = 1/5) is the only legend left that no desk mounts. Keep them as the specimen of a shape a desk may return to, or move kindOf/spokenTile to their own module and delete the rest.

## Flow
- grep the importers of CullTile / Zoom
- decide keep-as-specimen or delete; if delete, move kindOf, TileMedia, spokenTile first, then remove the components, their CSS and the kit rows, and amend INVENTORY

## Expected impact
A desk author reading INVENTORY stops reaching for a lens no screen mounts. Deleting could break the kit census and BoardKit.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no component whose only consumer is its specimen
Before: 2 components, 0 production mounts
After: 0 dead components, or a recorded reason to keep
Method: probe - importer grep
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: BlindPair's reduced-motion reveal (500 ms) is promised and never applied
instrument: a render test of BlindPair under an emulated prefers-reduced-motion (jsdom matchMedia stub or a tests/live page.emulateMedia) asserting the reveal time; arm B reads the media query in BlindPair's default or Board passes revealMs
body:
## Summary
REVEAL_MS's doc says "the prototype's 1150 ms; 500 reduced" and the prop says reduced motion is the caller's, but no caller passes `revealMs`.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/pair/BlindPair.tsx:29-30 and :40; app/(studio)/board/_board/Board.tsx:183 mounts BlindPair with no revealMs (grep -rn revealMs: only BlindPair.tsx). A reduced-motion operator waits 1150 ms per pair, during which `pick` refuses (line 77: revealing !== null).

## Flow
- emulate reduced motion, open a blind-pair packet, press 1
- the next pair arrives after 1150 ms, not 500

## Expected impact
Reduced-motion operators judge pairs ~2.3x faster between picks. Could break nothing pinned (tests pass revealMs: 0).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the reveal honours reduced motion as documented
Before: 0 callers pass revealMs; 1150 ms under reduced motion
After: 500 ms (predicted)
Method: simulation - Board.tsx:183 read; the gate needs a DOM (vitest runs in node) and the caller is out of scope
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none

title: A blind-pair pick is written while the packet's commit is in flight
instrument: a jsdom or live case: busy=true, press 1, assert onPick not called (arm B: `if (busy) return` in pick, as CutReview.end has)
body:
## Summary
BlindPair's `pick` guards a reveal and a judged pair but not `busy`, while CutReview's `end` refuses during a write.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/pair/BlindPair.tsx:76-80 vs packages/ui/src/components/cut/CutReview.tsx `end` ("A second press while a write or a preview is in flight is the same act again"). With a commit in flight (`busy`), 1/2/0/X still call onPick on the packet being committed.

## Flow
- judge every pair, press ⏎ (busy), press 1 before the write returns (after an undo)
- onPick fires against a committing packet

## Expected impact
No pick lands on a packet mid-commit. Could break nothing pinned.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - no pick during a commit in flight
Before: 0 busy guards in pick (CutReview: 1)
After: 1
Method: simulation - the press cannot be driven in the node vitest lane
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none

title: The cut review overflows at phone width: a 300px side column beside the player
instrument: cx-capture of a cut packet on the Board at --width 390 (fixture side), scrollWidth vs clientWidth; arm B stacks .cut under a width query
body:
## Summary
`.cut` is `minmax(0,1.5fr) minmax(var(--w-desk-side),1fr)` with no narrow layout; --w-desk-side is 300px.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/cut/Cut.module.css:4; tokens/source.json w-desk-side 300px. At 390px with sp-6 padding the player column is squeezed to ~0 and the page scrolls sideways. part-workspace-desk's Lane B card covers the Board's rail at phone width, not this grid.

## Flow
- open a cut packet at 390px
- the beats column holds 300px; the player collapses

## Expected impact
A cut is reviewable on a phone. Could shift the desktop layout if the query is wrong.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - no horizontal scroll at 390px
Before: predicted overflow (300px + padding in a 390px viewport)
After: stacked columns
Method: simulation - needs a dev server capture, which round-agents may not run
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none

title: The cut player skips the focused beat's seek when its metadata is not loaded yet
instrument: a live spec: press ↓ twice before the video's loadedmetadata, then assert currentTime == beat t0 after it loads; arm B re-seeks on loadedmetadata
body:
## Summary
The seek effect returns when `readyState === 0`, and nothing re-seeks once the video loads.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/cut/CutReview.tsx useEffect over [focus, beats]: `if (v !== null && b !== undefined && v.readyState > 0) v.currentTime = b.t0`. With preload="metadata" on a slow blob door, a beat chosen before metadata arrives is silently not sought.

## Flow
- open a cut, press ↓ at once
- the beat is focused, the player stays at 0:00

## Expected impact
The player always shows the focused beat. Could double-seek on a fast load.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the player follows the cursor
Before: 1 dropped seek per early move (walked)
After: 0
Method: simulation - needs a real media element
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none

title: Approve or Reject with a beat note open drops the typed note
instrument: a live spec: E on a beat, type, click Approve without ⏎, assert the verdict note carries the words (arm B: end() attaches the open draft first, as withNote reads it)
body:
## Summary
`end` builds the verdict note from `notes` only; a draft still in the open field is discarded.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/cut/CutReview.tsx `end` calls beatNote(beats, notes) and never reads `editing`/`text`. The A/R keys cannot fire from inside the field, but the Approve/Reject buttons can.

## Flow
- E on beat 2, type "tighter", click Approve
- the verdict lands with no note

## Expected impact
The reviewer's last words reach the step. Could attach a half-typed note the reviewer meant to drop.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a typed note is never lost on a verdict
Before: draft dropped (walked)
After: draft attached
Method: simulation - a click on a mounted button needs a DOM
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
